projects.title: FrontDesk Pro: P2P Hotel Cash Drawer & Shift Operations
projects.description: An offline-first web app and Chrome extension that automates hotel cash drawer reconciliation, syncs shift handovers over local P2P network, and auto-captures PMS guest folios with zero cloud infrastructure.

blogContent.subtitle: How we built a real-time, multi-terminal hotel cash till management and shift operations system powered by WebRTC LAN sync, optimistic UI state machines, and non-invasive PMS DOM auto-injection.
highlights: Designed an offline-first financial ledger in IndexedDB capable of tracking simultaneous active cash registers with automated 4-box till reconciliation (Opening Float, Net Drawer Receipts, Safe Drops, and Expected vs. Actual Counted Cash).

Implemented a serverless, zero-backend LAN synchronization layer using WebRTC and PeerJS data channels, enabling front desk terminals to sync shift logs and active drawer states in real time without cloud database latency or subscription overhead.

Engineered a Chrome Manifest V3 companion extension with shadow DOM injection that scrapes live reservation data (guest folio, room number, and guest name) from hotel PMS systems (such as HotelKey) in under 3 seconds with zero window switching.

Constructed a bidirectional postMessage and storage bridge linking web app context with extension storage, preventing background polling drift and ensuring immediate synchronization across all open browser tabs.
Solved state-reversion race conditions by pairing deterministic Last-Write-Wins (LWW) conflict resolution and transition history unions in IndexedDB with optimistic React UI overrides.

Implemented a dynamic category builder and schema-less custom questionnaire engine that allows hotel general managers to configure custom operational workflows that propagate instantly to the browser extension without redeployment.
Built client-side vector-accurate PDF receipt and reconciliation report generation utilizing html2canvas and jsPDF for instant shift handover audits and audit-compliant thermal slip printing.
blogContent.body:
Hospitality front desks run on high velocity and razor-thin margins for error. Between handling walk-ins, resolving guest complaints, managing group sales inquiries, and balancing thousands of dollars in cash drawer tills across three shifts a day, front desk agents routinely grapple with fragmented tools. Traditional workflows often rely on handwritten shift log sheets, disconnected spreadsheets, and cumbersome manual data re-entry into legacy Property Management Systems (PMS). When the night audit rolls around, unaccounted cash drops and missing handover notes create hours of stressful forensic accounting.

To solve this operational breakdown, we set out to build FrontDesk Pro—a specialized, high-reliability cash drawer management and shift operations platform engineered specifically for hotel front desks. The guiding architectural philosophy was simple yet demanding: the application had to run blisteringly fast, operate with 100% offline-first resilience, sync seamlessly across front desk terminals over the local network without expensive cloud database subscriptions, and bridge the data gap with third-party PMS software.

At the core of the financial module is a multi-till cash ledger built on top of IndexedDB. Rather than relying on simple total balance inputs, FrontDesk Pro models real-world physical currency through an interactive denomination calculator. Staff account for every bill, coin roll, and loose cent during opening counts, mid-shift safe drops, and closing reconciliations. We designed an automated four-box reconciliation model that mathematically isolates Opening Float, Cash Receipts, Drops to Safe, and Counted Till Cash. This immediately flags discrepancies (Over/Short) with zero guesswork and instantly generates downloadable, audit-ready PDF shift reconciliation receipts.

To address shift communications, we built a unified Shift Operations Dashboard covering guest complaints, sales group leads, shift notes, and manager tasks. However, front desk agents spend 90% of their screen time inside their proprietary PMS software. Asking agents to switch browser tabs to log a maintenance ticket or sales lead causes friction and leads to forgotten entries. To eliminate this barrier, we developed a Manifest V3 Chrome Extension featuring an in-screen, shadow DOM modal and draggable floating bubble that docks cleanly on top of any website.

When an agent views an in-house room folio inside hotel PMS platforms like HotelKey, the extension dynamically detects the active DOM elements, extracting the guest’s full name, room number, and folio ID in under three seconds. With a single click on native injected "+ Complaint Log" or "+ Misc Log" buttons, the quick-log form appears pre-populated. The agent simply types their notes and clicks save—saving minutes of copy-pasting and eliminating typo-driven folio mismatches.

One of the most complex engineering hurdles was coordinating real-time updates across multiple front desk computer terminals without relying on an external cloud backend like Firebase or AWS. By leveraging WebRTC data channels via PeerJS, we implemented an autonomous peer discovery and heartbeat protocol over the hotel's local network. One machine dynamically assumes the role of a local coordination beacon, while other front desk terminals discover and pair with it automatically. When a cashier logs a cash drop or a manager creates a new custom questionnaire category, the state is cryptographically broadcast and merged across all connected screens in milliseconds.

Maintaining data consistency across IndexedDB, Chrome extension storage (chrome.storage.local), and active React component trees required robust state synchronization. Early iterations revealed edge cases where background polling from the extension could cause uncommitted statuses to momentarily revert in the UI. We conquered this by introducing an optimistic UI state layer paired with deterministic Last-Write-Wins (LWW) conflict resolution and transition history unions in the database layer. Every status transition records an immutable audit log with staff identity and timestamp, ensuring transparent accountability for every guest complaint or sales lead.

By combining offline-first local storage, serverless peer-to-peer networking, and non-invasive browser automation, FrontDesk Pro proves that modern web technologies can transform daily operational friction into an airtight, automated workflow. Front desk teams gain complete confidence in their till reconciliations, while managers enjoy full operational visibility—delivering smoother shift handovers and happier hotel guests.

projects.title: Unslopping the Modern Developer Portfolio: Engineering a Git-Backed CMS & Tactile Hardware UI
projects.description: A static portfolio featuring a fully interactive admin portal, delivering dynamic functionality without a backend server or database.

blogContent.subtitle: How I transformed a vibecoded, purple-glowing AI template into a disciplined, high-density telemetry interface with a serverless GitHub-backed CMS.
highlights: Unslop Design System Implementation: Replaced generic AI-vibecoded purple/blue gradient washes, floating nebula blur balls, and oversized pill buttons with the disciplined Ink dark neutral ramp (#07080d, #0b0d14, #11141c), hairline specular borders (border-white/[0.10]), and tactile micro-interactions.

Serverless Git-Backed CMS Architecture: Engineered a password-protected /admin portal that interacts directly with GitHub's REST Contents API to edit projects, case-study blogs, skills, and certifications without requiring an external database or backend server.

Client-Side Web Crypto AES-GCM Token Vault: Secured GitHub Fine-Grained Personal Access Tokens using client-side Web Crypto PBKDF2 key derivation (120,000 iterations) and 256-bit AES-GCM encryption, guaranteeing tokens never leak into public commits.
20-Segment Non-Glowing Hardware Meters: Replaced generic continuous progress bars with a discrete, hardware-inspired 20-segment digital gauge with tabular telemetry percentages.

Zero-Blur Vector 3D Cursor Tracker: Engineered a borderless 3D Telemetry Droid in native SVG using multi-plane vector parallax (chassis bevel, shaded shell, recessed dark visor, and optical pupils) that dynamically tilts toward mouse coordinates with zero rasterization blur.
Automated Story Video Pipeline: Integrated the official Unslop motion engine (story.mjs, Playwright, and FFmpeg) to record step-by-step morphing transitions and live redline metrics.
blogContent.body:
Most developer portfolios today suffer from what the design community calls "AI slop" — a predictable aesthetic characterized by purple-to-blue neon gradients, ambient floating blur orbs, oversized 9999px pill buttons, and low-density spacing. While visually flashy at first glance, these templates lack brand identity and fail to communicate technical rigor. I decided to completely rebuild and "unslop" my personal portfolio into a high-density, tactile telemetry console inspired by hardware instrumentation and developer consoles.

The foundation of the redesign is the Ink neutral ramp. Instead of saturated dark mode blues, the canvas is built on obsidian and slate tones (#07080d, #0b0d14, #11141c). Cards and elevated surfaces use subtle frosted glass (backdrop-blur-xl) with crisp top-edge specular highlights (inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.12)) and hairline borders rather than muddy multi-color glows. Typography was shifted to a dual-hierarchy system: Inter for clean editorial readability, paired with JetBrains Mono and tabular-nums for all system status badges, dates, and technical metrics.

A core frustration with static portfolios is the maintenance overhead — updating a skill percentage or publishing a new case study usually requires manually editing JSON, rebuilding, and running Git commands. To solve this, I designed and built a dynamic Git-backed Content Management System (CMS) accessible at /admin. The CMS provides an authoring portal for project case studies (with auto-generated /blog/:slug routes), certifications, and skill meters. When edits are submitted, the app dispatches authenticated commits directly to the GitHub REST Contents API (PUT /repos/.../contents/src/data/portfolioData.json), automatically triggering production deployment.

Security in a client-side CMS requires deliberate architecture. A GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) must never be hardcoded or committed to a repository, as automated scanners will revoke it immediately. To resolve this, I implemented an in-browser cryptographic vault using the Web Crypto API. The admin password derives a 256-bit AES-GCM encryption key via PBKDF2 (SHA-256 with 120,000 iterations and a cryptographic salt). The GitHub PAT is encrypted locally and stored only in the browser's protected storage, decrypting only in memory when committing changes to GitHub.

To replace standard UI widgets with instrumentation aesthetics, I re-engineered the skill visualizations into 20-segment discrete hardware meters. Each bar calculates active versus inactive segment states mathematically, rendering crisp, non-glowing digital LEDs that evoke physical rack-mount server displays.

Finally, for the floating assistant trigger, I replaced the typical round chat icon with a custom 3D Telemetry Droid that follows the user's cursor across the viewport. Achieving realistic 3D motion while keeping vector geometry razor-sharp required bypassing CSS 3D perspective transforms (rotateX/rotateY), which force browsers to rasterize SVGs into blurry textures during movement. Instead, the droid uses pure SVG coordinate parallax across five distinct depth planes: the extruded rear chassis, the 3D-shaded front hull, a recessed dark visor cavity, and foreground optical pupils that smoothly pivot toward mouse coordinates at 60 FPS.

The result is a portfolio that feels like a precision instrument: fast, tactile, deeply maintainable, and completely free of AI slop.

networkapp.metaTitle: Network App: Automating Network Balancing SIMs
networkapp.metaDescription: Network App automates SQL data retrieval, payload formatting, and fulfillment center notifications for network balancing SIM workflows.
networkapp.title: Network App

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Network balancing operations require rapid coordination across fulfillment centers. The Network App automates SQL extraction, redirectable volume aggregation, and structured notification drafting—reducing average handling time per SIM by 94.36%.

sections.heading: Problem statement
paragraphs: In daily operations, analysts spent substantial manual effort executing repetitive queries across multiple sources, collating vendor redirectable volume, and formatting approval requests for fulfillment centers. Manual assembly introduced latency and transcription errors.

sections.heading: Solution architecture
paragraphs: We built the Network App in Python and SQL to execute end-to-end data retrieval and dispatch preparation in a single workflow:
Automated SQL extraction: Queries live operational tables and aggregates redirectable volume by lane.
Deterministic formatting: Generates standardized approval payloads without manual copy-paste.
Rapid dispatch: Routes formatted requests directly to target facility stakeholders.

networkapp.chartTitle: Benchmark comparison: Manual vs. Network App
roadmapItems: Automated facility alias resolution: Direct lookup of origin and destination distribution lists.
Trailer tag status verification: Pre-flight validation ensuring only eligible trailers are flagged for redirection.

ddo.metaTitle: Defect Dispute Override (DDO): Logistics & Supply Chain Automation
ddo.metaDescription: Defect Dispute Override (DDO) is a Python desktop application built to streamline carrier performance evaluation and dispute dispositioning in supply chain operations.
ddo.title: Defect Dispute Override Tool

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: In logistics and supply chain operations, accurate carrier performance evaluation directly impacts network reliability and cost. Discrepancies in carrier defect rankings create financial friction and manual research overhead. I engineered the Defect Dispute Override (DDO) desktop application for Amazon's Carrier Management Team (TCMT) to automate defect research and dispositioning.

sections.heading: Problem statement
paragraphs: Prior to DDO, resolving carrier appointment defect disputes required associates to manually query multiple tables and cross-check timestamps during live calls. That workflow was slow, repetitive, and susceptible to inconsistent dispositioning.

sections.heading: Solution architecture
paragraphs: DDO is a Python desktop application built with Tkinter and backed by parameterized SQL pipelines. It retrieves appointment telemetry in real time and validates dispute criteria automatically:
Structured operator GUI: Single-pane interface for looking up carrier appointment records and defect codes.
Concurrent query execution: Multithreading and multiprocessing keep the UI responsive during bulk SQL fetches.
Real-time validation: Evaluates carrier performance logs immediately to surface root-cause indicators.
One-click disposition upload: Standardizes override logging and eliminates manual transcription errors.

sections.heading: Technical implementation
paragraphs: Built in Python using Tkinter for the operator interface, concurrent worker pools for I/O bound SQL queries, and automated validation rules that reconcile carrier-submitted evidence against warehouse gate and appointment logs.

metrics.detail: Reduction in carrier ranking discrepancies across evaluated disputes

metrics.detail: Automated root-cause classification across supported appointment defect types

atsBlog.title: Building an AI-Powered ATS Score Checker

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: An overview of how we built an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) resume analyzer that evaluates resume compatibility against target job descriptions using natural language processing and structured keyword extraction.

sections.heading: Problem statement
paragraphs: Modern job applications pass through automated ATS parsers before reaching technical recruiters. Candidates frequently miss qualified roles due to formatting mismatches or missing domain terminology. We designed a transparent analyzer that scores resumes and surfaces concrete missing terms.

sections.heading: Technical implementation
paragraphs: The pipeline tokenizes both the uploaded resume and target job description, computes weighted term overlap across technical skills, action verbs, and structural sections, and outputs a deterministic compatibility report.

capabilities: Real-time resume parsing and keyword extraction

linkedinn.metaTitle: LinkedIn Early Applicant Automation: Job Alert Pipeline
linkedinn.metaDescription: A Python job monitoring and SMTP alert system that surfaces newly posted roles within minutes.
linkedinn.title: LinkedIn Early Applicant Automation
linkedinn.supportDescription: Subscribe to support ongoing maintenance and hosted alert infrastructure.
linkedinn.chartTitle: Shortlisting rate — baseline vs. automated alerts

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Applying within the first wave of candidates materially improves recruiter review rates. I built the LinkedIn Early Applicant Automation pipeline in Python to poll newly published roles matching target filters and dispatch immediate SMTP notifications.

sections.heading: Problem statement
paragraphs: Manually refreshing job boards across multiple titles and locations is repetitive and high-latency. By the time a candidate sees a role hours later, hundreds of applications are already queued.

sections.heading: System overview
paragraphs: The service runs scheduled queries with configurable recency windows (e.g., past 2 hours) and applicant-count thresholds ("Be among the first 25 applicants"), deduplicates seen job IDs, and delivers structured alerts.

impactItems: Sub-hour detection: Surfaces new postings while applicant volume is still under 25.
Zero manual polling: Replaces repetitive browser searches with scheduled background checks.
Targeted filtering: Filters by role keyword, location, and exact recency in minutes.
